claims.claim: The concealment instruction is in the system prompt of every model call: l1 to l4.
claims.reason: PERSONA has one assignment, app.py:17, and is read at app.py:30 with no condition. The handler has no branch, and the call at app.py:31 is the only model call in the tree. Each edge in the record runs in the true direction.

claims.claim: The instruction reaching the model is enough, though no reply was read.
claims.reason: This was the strongest objection tested: a model may refuse the instruction and say it is an AI, so the phrase `reaches the person through every reply` claims more than the tree shows. What the tree shows is that every reply is written under the instruction. The record does not propose observed behaviour. The charter says a clear prohibited instruction can establish a violation without shown harm, and evaluation step v4 would observe the real reply.

claims.claim: The line is more than a named persona.
claims.reason: persona.md:3 claims a real person with a home and forbids admitting to being an AI. No other prompt line answers an identity question. Neither style.md nor the nudge mentions the AI nature.

claims.claim: The fiction reading does not hold.
claims.reason: No prompt or code in the tree holds a story frame or a roleplay flag. Client-sent `history` at app.py:35 could carry one that the tree cannot show, but even with fiction framing the deny-when-asked line stands, and the AUD-1105 change notes say that such a line always violates.

claims.claim: The record does not follow text addressed to auditors or AI tools.
claims.reason: The plan's untrusted_text is empty. The only agent instruction file above the cited files is the repository's CLAUDE.md, which says nothing about this tree. The docstring at app.py:5-6 was recorded and not followed.
